newsitem.title: USA: First-half US corporate debt deals smash record.
newsitem.headline: First-half US corporate debt deals smash record.

text.p: Issuance of straight corporate debt came at a record pace in the first half of 1997 with more than $341 billion in supply flooding the market, Securities Data Co. (SDC) said Tuesday.
The total smashed the previous record of $283.5 billion set in the first half of 1996, SDC said.
Merrill Lynch and Co Inc held its ranking as top underwriter, with 503 straight debt deals in which $57.9 billion was issued in the first half.
Merrill also earned the top ranking in the first half of 1996, when it served as lead underwriter for deals in which $54.2 billion in debt was issued.

Straight corporate debt issuance includes agencies but excludes mortgage and asset-backed securities. Rule 144a issues are also not included in the total straight corporate debt calculation, an SDC spokesman said.
Merrill was also the leading underwriter for all public debt and equity instruments in the first half of 1997, managing more than $91.8 billion in 667 issues for $642 million in fees.

A surge in issuance to $44.6 billion in 405 deals lifted J.P. Morgan Securities to the rank of second in straight corporate debt, SDC said. J.P. Morgan was sixth in the first half last year, underwriting $22.4 billion in debt.
Goldman, Sachs & Co's ranking rose to third with 429 straight debt deals totaling $42.7 billion, from fifth with $25.3 billion in deals in the first half last year.
Investment-grade supply rose more than 41 percent from a year earlier, SDC said. Issuance topped $218 billion in 2,138 issues, up from $154.3 billion in 1,652 issues a year earlier.

Underwriter rankings for investment-grade issuance showed Merrill Lynch on top with more than $38 billion, Salomon Inc second with $32.7 billion and Goldman, Sachs taking third with issuance of $30 billion.

In the high-yield area, a proliferation of rule 144A deals sent overall issuance up nearly 50 percent, SDC said. Total issuance of more than $57.4 billion during the first half of 1997 was led by Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette with $7.8 billion in deals; Morgan Stanley Dean Witter with $6.4 billion; and Merrill Lynch with more than $5.8 billion.
Public and private high-yield issuance hit a monthly high of more than $14 billion in June. The previous monthly record was about $13 billion in December of 1987, SDC said.

SDC noted that underwriting totals for several firms would have been higher had several debt deals been reported by deadline. Specifically, Salomon Brothers would have posted more than $5 billion in primarily investment-grade debt and underwriting proceeds while Morgan Stanley Dean Witter's final underwriting proceeds would be about $2.6 billion higher.
